items.answer: The daily work of a store manager illustrates all five of Fayol's functions

items.stem: A student claims: "A leadership style that works in one country will work everywhere." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: National cultures differ in attitudes to authority, communication and teamwork, so styles must be adapted.
items.markingKey: National cultures differ in attitudes to authority, communication and teamwork, so styles must be adapted. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Read the extract.

After buying Twitter in 2022, Elon Musk cut about 80% of staff and told employees to commit to being "extremely hardcore" or leave.

Analyse the significance of autocratic leadership for the organization(s) in the extract. [4]
items.answer: Rapid top-down decisions cut costs quickly but damaged morale, trust and relations with advertisers
items.markingKey: Rapid top-down decisions cut costs quickly but damaged morale, trust and relations with advertisers [1]-[2]: relevant points with limited use of the extract; [3]-[4]: clear analysis explicitly linked to the extract.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Leadership is more important than management for the success of a business."
items.answer: Both are essential: leadership matters most in times of change and innovation, management in stable, efficiency-driven operations.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: vision and motivation drive innovation; leaders guide change; culture and engagement. Arguments against: without planning and control, resources are wasted; routine operations depend on management; depends on the situation and industry. Supported judgement: Both are essential: leadership matters most in times of change and innovation, management in stable, efficiency-driven operations.

items.stem:
As CEO of PepsiCo (2006-2018), Indra Nooyi introduced "Performance with Purpose", shifting the portfolio towards healthier products and sustainability goals.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that ethical leadership is more important than profitability for long-term business success. [8]
items.answer: Ethical leadership and long-term profitability are complementary; firms that sacrifice ethics for short-term profit, like Volkswagen or Enron, often destroy value.
items.markingKey: Advantages: trust and reputation; lower legal risks; employee engagement. Disadvantages: without profit the firm cannot survive; shareholder pressure for returns; ethical choices may raise costs. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

items.stem:
The Tata Group in India built townships, hospitals and schools for workers, beginning with Jamsetji Tata's steel works at Jamshedpur in the early 1900s.

The management team is divided. One manager argues that there is no single best leadership style. Evaluate this view and recommend a course of action. [10]
items.answer: Effective leaders adapt their style to the situation, although democratic approaches generally suit knowledge-based organizations.
items.markingKey: Supporting: situational theory: depends on task and followers; crises need autocratic decisions; experts need autonomy. Challenging: democratic leadership generally improves engagement; consistency of style builds trust; culture may favour one style. Recommendation: Effective leaders adapt their style to the situation, although democratic approaches generally suit knowledge-based organizations. Read the extract.

Define the term "laissez-faire leadership". [2]
items.answer: A style in which the leader gives employees a high degree of freedom to make decisions and organize their work, with minimal interference
items.markingKey: [2] for a full, accurate definition: a style in which the leader gives employees a high degree of freedom to make decisions and organize their work, with minimal interference. [1] for a partial definition. Examples alone are not credited.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "leadership"?
options: A leadership style in which the leader makes decisions alone and expects employees to follow instructions, with little consultation
The process of achieving organizational objectives by planning, organizing, commanding, coordinating and controlling resources
Monitoring performance against targets and taking corrective action when needed
The ability to influence, inspire and motivate others to work towards achieving goals
items.answer: The ability to influence, inspire and motivate others to work towards achieving goals
items.markingKey: D. "leadership" is the ability to influence, inspire and motivate others to work towards achieving goals.

items.stem: Which researcher developed the cultural dimensions of power distance and individualism?
items.answer: Geert Hofstede
items.markingKey: Geert Hofstede. Hofstede's cultural dimensions theory.

items.stem: Explain the difference between democratic leadership and autocratic leadership.
items.answer: Autocratic leaders make decisions alone and give instructions; democratic leaders consult and involve employees in decisions.
items.markingKey: Autocratic leaders make decisions alone and give instructions; democratic leaders consult and involve employees in decisions. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why controlling is an important function of management.
items.answer: Without monitoring performance against targets, problems such as overspending or falling quality are not detected and corrected in time.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Without monitoring performance against targets, problems such as overspending or falling quality are not detected and corrected in time. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between ethical leadership and legal compliance.
items.answer: Ethical leadership is guided by moral principles beyond the law; legal compliance simply means obeying the law.
items.markingKey: Ethical leadership is guided by moral principles beyond the law; legal compliance simply means obeying the law. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A hospital emergency department faces a sudden major incident. Explain which leadership style is most appropriate and why.
items.answer: An autocratic style is most appropriate: decisions must be made quickly and clearly under pressure, with clear lines of command. Consultation would waste time; afterwards a more democratic style could be used to review the response.
items.markingKey: An autocratic style is most appropriate: decisions must be made quickly and clearly under pressure, with clear lines of command. Consultation would waste time; afterwards a more democratic style could be used to review the response.

items.stem: Using Jacinda Ardern's Covid-19 response as an example, explain situational leadership.
items.answer: New Zealand's Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern combined fast, firm decisions in March 2020 with clear, empathetic daily communication. She adapted her style, being directive in the crisis while consulting experts and building public trust
items.markingKey: Context (New Zealand's Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern combined fast, firm decisions in March 2020 with clear, empathetic daily communication.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: A student claims: "Every manager is automatically a good leader." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Managers have formal authority, but leadership requires the ability to influence and inspire, which not all managers have; leaders can also exist without formal positions.
items.markingKey: Managers have formal authority, but leadership requires the ability to influence and inspire, which not all managers have; leaders can also exist without formal positions. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.
